title: Excluded-Mass Relative Error for Side-Channel Security
summary: Ordinary worst-case relative error is maximal for Gaussian-noisy Hamming-weight leakage; re-deriving affected security results with excluded-mass relative error remains open.

formal_statement.body:
For Hamming-weight leakage with additive Gaussian noise, the ordinary worst-case relative error $\operatorname{RE}(X;Y)$ reaches its maximal value $|\mathcal{X}|-1$ because arbitrarily unlikely outputs can determine the supremum. For an exclusion budget $E$, define
$$
\operatorname{RE}_{E}(X;Y):=\inf_{\substack{A\subseteq\mathcal{Y}\\ \Pr[Y\in A^{c}]\le E}} \sup_{y\in A} \sup_{x\in\mathcal{X}}\left|\frac{p_{Y\mid X}(y\mid x)}{p_Y(y)}-1\right|,
$$
so that at most $E$ probability mass is excluded. Develop and prove $\operatorname{RE}_{E}$-based analogues of all side-channel security results whose hypotheses or conclusions use ordinary $\operatorname{RE}$.

scope.domain: Relative-error analysis of side-channel security for noisy Hamming-weight leakage.
assumptions: The leakage is Hamming-weight leakage with additive Gaussian noise.
parameters: E: exclusion budget limiting the probability mass removed from consideration
scope.unresolved_remainder: Develop and prove excluded-mass-relative-error analogues of all side-channel security results whose hypotheses or conclusions use ordinary relative error.

citations.label: Formal Security Proofs via Doeblin Coefficients: Optimal Side-channel Factorization from Noisy Leakage to Random Probing

progress.summary: The source introduces excluded-mass relative error as a potential fix for domination by extremely unlikely outputs. It states that adopting this patch would require re-deriving all results in terms of the new definition.
citation_labels: Julien Béguinot et al., Formal Security Proofs via Doeblin Coefficients: Optimal Side-channel Factorization from Noisy Leakage to Random Probing
